central_question: What changes when VERIFY THE WORLD leaves JANUS and tests the frozen music map against independent sources?
most_important_confirmations: Alan Parsons himself states Sirius was changed in key to make it an intro to Eye in the Sky.
The deliberate Phil Spector / Wall of Sound design of Don't Answer Me is externally documented.
I Robot's Synthi-A sequencer programming and choir are directly documented by official credits.
Ammonia Avenue's industrial-plant origin and science/public misunderstanding theme are directly documented.
Pink Floyd Time clock recordings and Money's measured seven-beat tape loop survive first-person verification.
most_important_falsifications_or_demotio: Don't Answer Me: B-flat-major / I-vi-IV-V description does not survive; licensed metadata gives C major and common transcriptions give C-Am-Dm-G at the opening.
Don't Answer Me video: Michael Patterson attribution does not survive; Mike Kaluta/Broadcast Arts is the supported line.
In the Lap of the Gods: harpsichord and blanket wordless-choir claims do not survive official credits / Parsons recollection.
Lucifer: C-minor, repeated-C-center, and clavinet/wah claims do not survive; the instrument claim is demonstrably cross-track contamination inside Eve.
Ammonia Avenue: sax-to-guitar relay and Christopher Rainbow-as-sax claims do not survive official credits.
Pink Floyd Time: pencil-held multiple-loop story is not supported in checked first-person sources.
Pink Floyd Money: exact fixed 7.5-inch segment law is not supported.
why_this_is_epistemically_better_than_an: Independent sources can falsify attractive details that an internally coherent semantic graph would tend to preserve.
Official credits distinguish instruments that semantic listening can easily confuse, as demonstrated by Lucifer versus neighboring Eve tracks.
Licensed score metadata constrains keys and removes arbitrary transposition ambiguity.
First-person production recollections constrain studio anecdotes and expose story conflation between Time and Money.

new_difference_operator.witness_A: Frozen user/JANUS music-mechanics map before external search.
new_difference_operator.witness_B: Independent official, licensed and first-person external evidence.
new_difference_operator.lesson: A useful semantic formula is allowed to survive even when one or more of its supporting technical decorations are false.

support: Sirius was actually adapted to function as the intro to Eye in the Sky.
I Robot actually combines sequenced electronics with human choral and live-band elements.
Don't Answer Me actually uses intentional production-style contrast through Spector-like Wall of Sound.
Ammonia Avenue actually combines human-scale songwriting with documented industrial/scientific subject matter and orchestral/guitar production.
